literal: Like wealth with him who has envy, there is no greatness with him who lacks good conduct.
translation: Just as there is no lasting prosperity in a person filled with envy, there can be no true greatness in one who lacks right conduct.
modern: பொறாமை உடையவனிடத்தில் செல்வம் நிலைக்காதது போல, நல்லொழுக்கம் இல்லாதவனிடத்தில் உயர்வு இருக்காது.
explanation: This couplet uses a powerful comparison to show that right conduct is indispensable for personal elevation. The poet states that just as wealth (ஆக்கம்) cannot truly exist or flourish in an envious person (அழுக்காறு உடையான்), true greatness (உயர்வு) cannot exist in someone who lacks proper conduct (ஒழுக்கம் இலான்). The locative suffix 'கண்' is used to denote the locus of these qualities. By linking the impossibility of wealth in the envious to the impossibility of greatness in the undisciplined, the verse highlights that moral character is the sole foundation for any real rise in life.
